experiment: DCF-19 regime-level routing on the DCF-15 mesh
world: identical to DCF-15 (mesh15.py, its PROTOCOL.json and cost_model15.json are used unchanged)
policy: regime: at each slow-epoch start t in {8,16,24}, every episode in the batch uses exact if the batch mean of S = sum over pending cross-unit sensors of (ln 2 - H(e)) is >= tau, else cluster BP; epoch 0 uses BP
baselines: fixed_bp (strongest dev-selected policy in DCF-15), fixed_exact; epoch_oracle picks the better operator per batch-epoch with hindsight (privileged upper bound for this policy class)
accounting: one kernel launch per step: a_op + b_op * summed work (DCF-15 calibrated model), plus block-update kernel; routing time = measured wall time of computing S, spread over the epoch's queries
tau_selection: maximise mean objective_total over the four DCF-15 development conditions (rho 0.2/0.4 x noise low/high, DCF-15 dev seeds); ties go to the larger tau

gates.R1: regime objective_total exceeds fixed_bp in more held-out conditions than it falls below (6 conditions, fresh seeds never used by DCF-15)
gates.R2: regime objective_total is within 0.001 of the better of fixed_bp and fixed_exact in at least 4 of 6 held-out conditions

equivalence: operator choice does not change mesh state, so the outcome of every policy is computed from a trace that executes both operators on every query (tests/test_regime19.py checks trace evaluation against a direct online run)
no_tuning: selection19.json is committed before trace19_test.json.gz is generated
